# EnterpriseGlue v0.18.0 Release Notes

Generated from release-note fragments changed since `v0.17.2`.

## Highlights

- **frontend-host:** Validates list API responses at the boundary so an unexpected non-array payload becomes an actionable query error instead of an opaque runtime TypeError or a misleading empty list.
- **frontend-runtime-config:** Adds backward-compatible container-start configuration of the browser API base URL so one frontend image can be promoted across environments without rebuilding it.

## User and administrator impact

- A list endpoint returning a non-array payload (an error envelope, an object, or a string) now enters the screen's normal request-error state instead of crashing the view with `TypeError: ... is not a function` or pretending the collection is empty.
- Developers get a typed `ListResponseContractError` plus a console diagnostic naming the request and describing the payload shape, so API contract mismatches, missing endpoints, and auth or configuration problems are identifiable without hand-instrumenting the code.
- Native tenant selection, tenant administration, tenant membership, and tenant discovery-domain lists use the same response validation as the other frontend list screens.
- Operators can promote one frontend image digest across test, acceptance, and production and select a browser-visible API origin when each container starts.
- Existing deployments remain unchanged when the new runtime variables are unset: the generated document applies no override and the frontend continues to use VITE_API_BASE_URL, then same-origin API paths.
- The production image generates and serves a same-origin runtime document and adds a validated cross-origin API origin to its Content Security Policy when configured.

## Upgrade and compatibility

- No action is required: when EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_API_BASE_URL is unset, the standard image behaves as before (VITE_API_BASE_URL, then same-origin).
- To opt in on Docker or OpenShift, set EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_API_BASE_URL on the frontend container to an absolute HTTP(S) URL and optionally set EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_CONFIG_REQUIRED=true. Prefer API_UPSTREAM when the browser can keep using same-origin API paths.
- Custom static deployments may continue to set VITE_RUNTIME_CONFIG_URL at build time to a same-origin JSON document containing apiBaseUrl and optional required fields.

## API and integration compatibility

- Adds `expectArray(value, context)`, `ListResponseContractError`, and `fetchList<T>(url, params?, options?, context?)` to `@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` `shared/api`; the existing `apiClient` surface is unchanged and valid array responses retain their existing behavior.

## Configuration

- No configuration or settings changes. The Email Configurations admin page is touched only by the list-response validation refactor (its list fetch now routes through `fetchList`); operators need take no action and no environment variables, settings, or config bundles change.
- New optional container variable EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_API_BASE_URL: an absolute HTTP(S) browser API base URL written into the standard image's same-origin runtime document when the container starts.
- New optional container variable EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_CONFIG_REQUIRED: when true, a missing or unusable runtime API value is a fatal frontend boot error; default false.
- The standard image builds with VITE_RUNTIME_CONFIG_URL=/.well-known/enterpriseglue/runtime-config.json; custom static deployments may override that build-time pointer and VITE_RUNTIME_CONFIG_REQUIRED.
- Precedence is runtime document, then VITE_API_BASE_URL, then same-origin; the runtime document is fetched with no-store so a restarted deployment takes effect immediately.

## Database migrations

- Database rollback supported for the combined release: yes.

## Security

- Unexpected payloads are described by type and key names in all environments; the full payload body is logged only in development builds, so production logs do not capture unexpected response contents.
- The configuration document is confined to the application's own origin; cross-origin and protocol-relative configuration pointers are rejected before any request is issued.
- Runtime API values are validated as absolute HTTP(S) URLs without credentials, query strings, or fragments before they are applied. The container entrypoint accepts only a restricted injection-safe URL character set.
- The HTTP interceptor derives its request allow-list from the validated API base URL, and the production entrypoint adds only that URL's origin to Content Security Policy connect-src.
- A cross-origin API must still permit the frontend origin through CORS and use cookie attributes appropriate for credentialed cross-origin requests.

## Known limitations

- Coverage is limited to GET list endpoints routed through `fetchList`; non-array `POST` responses and array data arriving via WebSocket/SSE or plugin bridges are not yet guarded, though `expectArray` is exported for incremental reuse.
- `null` and `undefined` list responses retain the existing compatibility behavior and resolve to an empty array; only truthy non-array contract violations become typed errors.
- Only apiBaseUrl and required are consumed from the runtime document today; unknown keys are ignored for forward compatibility.
- Custom static configuration documents must be reachable before the first API request; a slow endpoint delays startup, and a required unreachable endpoint blocks startup by design.
- Cross-origin APIs require coordinated CORS and cookie configuration; same-origin API_UPSTREAM remains the recommended container deployment.

## Rollback

- Redeploy the previous frontend image or `@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` package; no configuration or database rollback is required.
- Unset EG_FRONTEND_RUNTIME_API_BASE_URL and restart the frontend container to return to build-time or same-origin configuration; no image rebuild, data rollback, or schema rollback is required.
- Custom static deployments can unset VITE_RUNTIME_CONFIG_URL in their next build to disable the loader entirely.

## Validation evidence

- Frontend unit tests cover `expectArray` (arrays, null/undefined, typed contract errors, error envelopes, string and object payloads) and `fetchList` (array pass-through, non-array rejection with logged context, explicit context, and argument forwarding).
- `@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit`) and repository ESLint (`--max-warnings=0`) are clean over the changed files.
- Frontend runtime tests cover feature-off compatibility, successful no-store application, document-level required mode, unknown keys, transport/shape failures, same-origin pointer enforcement, and rejection of scheme-less, non-HTTP(S), credential-bearing, query-bearing, and malformed values.
- A deployment contract test verifies the stable image pointer, generated JSON, CSP substitution, Docker Compose, published-image self-hosting, OpenShift wiring, operator examples, and configuration matrix.
- Frontend host typecheck/build, production frontend build, frontend unit tests, Compose rendering, documentation boundary, release-note preflight, and published-package version discipline.
